annotations.text:
The ending is the board

No podium. At the whistle the board the band already opens comes up by itself and grows a head and a foot: the line saying who took it, the bar with each side's name inside its own share of it, the pilot list with your own row washed, and a foot carrying the countdown and one key.

One layout at every window size. Only the measure, the type and where the block sits change: 720 points on a monitor, the full width between the margins on a phone, and on an upright phone the block hugs the foot of the screen so the one key on it is under a thumb. The three boards across this page differ in one thing only, how the list is ordered.

Gone from the first four: the clock's drain bar, the block of big figures, the six SAY chips, and the share key that ran the width of the page. INVITE FRIEND is the same act as SHARE MATCH named for what a player wants out of it, and sized like a key.

One list, winner first

The board's own list, re-ordered once: the side that took it runs first, whether or not it is yours, so the line, the bar and the rows all read the same way down the page. Each name keeps its side's color and your own row stays washed wherever it lands.

Cost: mid-match the band puts your side on the left and this puts the winner there, so the one screen that changes the rule is the one you read after losing.

A block per side

The same rows, grouped, with each side's points on its own head. The team reading is unmistakable and a four-a-side game gets two short blocks rather than one run of eight.

Cost: two heads and a gap, which is the busiest of the three, and it says the score a third time after the bar and the numbers on it.

Best gun first

One list across both sides, ordered by kills, so the room is ranked and where you placed is where your washed row sits. This is the reading the shooters Chris pointed at are after: not who won, but who did well.

Cost: the sides interleave, so the team reading is only the colors, and a losing pilot can top the board, which is either the point or a provocation.

The first four directions, kept for the record. Chris's reading: too small and busy on a monitor, no sense of how you did, and mostly the scoreboard's content a second time. The page beside this one is what those notes came to.
